59 engagements

Ownership, governance and succession should be designed together, before the next generation needs them.

Family offices and high-net-worth clients account for 59 of the 650+ engagements in HAYKALAH’s archive census, 2004–2026. We structure how families hold, govern and pass on their assets, design family and charitable waqfs, and find the land and buildings that cost more to hold than they earn. Every conversation can start under an NDA, and no family is named without written consent.

Archive census counts are indicative.

What we do

  • Holding and governance structures for family groups and their companies.

  • Succession and continuity planning across jurisdictions.

  • Family and charitable waqf design, with nazir governance.

  • Portfolio reviews that find idle land and under-used buildings.

  • Real-estate structuring from raw land to an income-producing asset.

  • Screening of co-investment opportunities with HOAM.

  • One dashboard that reports the whole portfolio.

How we create value

  • 02

    Monetization

    Portfolio reviews identify the idle land and under-used buildings that the asset-monetization engine can put to work for recurring income.

  • 04

    Automation

    One dashboard reports the family’s whole portfolio of companies and assets, with live KPIs in place of manual reports.

  • 05

    Transformation

    For a Saudi family, HAYKALAH proposed a family and charitable waqf in 2021, with a nine-month plan to establish it, coordinate its advisers and seat the first nazir board.

Questions

Who does HAYKALAH coordinate in a family structure?

The family’s legal, Shariah, tax-and-Zakat and accounting advisers, who work to one plan that HAYKALAH manages.

Does HAYKALAH screen co-investments for families?

Yes. HOAM, the HAYKALAH Opportunity Assessment Matrix, scores a new opportunity on six axes against two decades of precedent. It is a screening tool, not investment advice.

Start with a confidential conversation about the family’s assets. An NDA can come first.
